definitions.explanation: The act of copying or imitating someone or something, whether in art, behavior, or technique. Often carries a neutral or slightly negative nuance, suggesting a lack of originality. Can be used as a suru-verb. Composed of 模 (model/pattern) + 倣 (emulate).

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{大人|おとな}を{模倣|もほう}して{学|まな}ぶ。
この{作品|さくひん}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{画家|がか}の{模倣|もほう}にすぎない。
examples.english: This work is nothing more than an imitation of a famous painter.

examples.japanese: {模倣|もほう}{犯罪|はんざい}を{防|ふせ}ぐために、{報道|ほうどう}の{仕方|しかた}にも{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Care must be taken in how things are reported in order to prevent copycat crimes.

notes:
USAGE:
{模倣|もほう} is more formal than {真似|まね} (imitation/mimicry). It is commonly used in academic, artistic, and media contexts. It can function as a suru-verb: {模倣|もほう}する (to imitate).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {模倣|もほう}する (to imitate)
- {模倣|もほう}{犯罪|はんざい} (copycat crime)
- {模倣|もほう}{品|ひん} (imitation product, counterfeit)
- {模倣|もほう}{者|しゃ} (imitator)
- {模倣|もほう}から{始|はじ}まる (start from imitation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{真似|まね} is the everyday word for "imitation" or "mimicry" and is less formal. {模写|もしゃ} specifically refers to copying a painting or artwork. {偽造|ぎぞう} means "forgery" or "counterfeiting" and implies illegal intent.
